newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Activists push ASEAN to ditch pact with Burma.
newsitem.headline: Activists push ASEAN to ditch pact with Burma.

text.p: Human rights activists in Malaysia on Friday pressed members of ASEAN to ditch their policy of "constructive engagement" with Burma.

"The so-called ASEAN constructive engagement policy has failed in putting a rein on the Burmese military junta," said Fan Yew Teng, spokesman for some 30 activists representing the Burma Solidarity Group Malaysia.
"Instead the junta has taken it as a green light to commit further human rights abuses," Fan told reporters after staging a brief demonstration outside the Malaysian foreign ministry.

In a memorandum to Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Badawi, the activists urged him to work for an immediate halt to human rights violations by Burma's ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).
Abdullah is meeting other foreign ministers of ASEAN (Association of South East Asian Nations) in Singapore on Saturday, following the conclusion of a conference between the European Union and ASEAN.
ASEAN, which groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam, plans to admit Burma into its fold soon, probably this year.
Burma's human rights record is condemned by the West, but ASEAN has initiated "constructive engagement" with Rangoon in the belief that the move will eventually coax the military rulers to reform.
Fan said ASEAN should try to arrange a genuine dialogue between the SLORC and the National League of Democracy led by Aung San Suu Kyi.
